study.question: Does preserving target/context-conditioned activation mass in field-wise history summary units recover click discrimination lost by unit-normalized summaries, beyond history count and a different attention kernel?
study.hypothesis: Observed: all four preceding single-seed variants execute successfully but trail baseline-din click AUC 0.655544. Field retrieval improves event retrieval by 0.000528 with feedback grouping and 0.001201 without it. Grouping lowers click AUC by 0.005860 (field) and 0.005187 (event), despite improved auxiliary task AUCs over DIN. The best preceding unified variant g0-r0000-field_global reaches 0.646474, with history_1_16 AUC 0.591524 versus DIN 0.614321 and history_gt64 0.653470 versus DIN 0.657803. No prior candidate diagnostics or repetitions establish why. Code inspection shows each field summary is normalized to unit total weight and separately receives log exposure/group counts. Hypothesis: counts do not preserve target-dependent activation mass. A field summary represented as a bounded gated sum may retain both content and target-conditioned magnitude, improving click ranking. This is a provisional explanation, not a conclusion from those unequal-architecture comparisons. DIN already motivates unnormalized pooling; the contribution sought here is controlled local evidence about field summary representation, not invention of that idea.

nearest_work.difference: Archived exact-version primary text, lines 250-277, explicitly motivates unnormalized local activation to retain interest intensity. Inherit that known motivation; use bounded sigmoid dot-product gates for each field with target/context queries in the existing unified token model, rather than DIN signed MLP event activations. No originality claim for unnormalized pooling or exact DIN reproduction.

Pinned benchmark implementation lines 80-145 pools whole item/action events, tokenizes pooled fields and task tokens, then uses HiFormer blocks. Keep our preceding field-specific context queries, shared small attention blocks and direct summary/static readout; vary only retrieval normalization. Original HiFormer paper detail unavailable through paper:hiformer, so equivalence and priority remain unverified.

Pinned benchmark implementation lines 112-158 uses target-pooled fields with global/chunk group tokens, reversible mixing and mean readout. No reversible transport or global/group tokenizer is adopted. It is a considered architectural alternative rather than a locally measured control. Original method text unavailable through paper:tokenmixer.

Exact local architectural parent. All embeddings, queries, keys, five summary slots, group counts/absence flags, 32-dimensional projections, two attention blocks, task identities, direct static/summary path and towers remain. Only the deterministic mapping of existing field retrieval scores to weights changes. softmax_reference is a prospective faithful rerun.

study.proposed_difference: For existing score s[b,f,t], define g=sigmoid(s) times the original binary retrieval mask, M=sum_t g, N=sum_t mask, and v=sum_t g*x. mass_sum uses v; mass_normalized uses v/max(M,1e-9); count_scaled uses (N/2)*v/max(M,1e-9); softmax_reference retains the exact original masked softmax. In all arms every field has its own gate and pooled content. The action embedding uses the average field weights, exactly as before. Count-scaled pooling has mass N/2, equal to sigmoid-sum mass at score zero, providing a target-independent magnitude control. Gate-normalized and sum arms use the same sigmoid kernel and tensor shapes. No new trainable tensors: expected parameters 32110916 total / 31793216 embeddings / 317700 dense, to be measured by the host. Field retrieval stays true and feedback_groups false in all arms. Existing group absence flags, counts, repeated summary slots and zero-length paths stay unchanged to avoid introducing another intervention. This narrowly tests a representation property after reviewing a failed direction; it does not establish a new unified architecture or isolate the earlier grouping failure.
predictions: Primary prospective contrast: mass_sum should improve full-population validation click AUC over count_scaled if target-dependent mass contributes beyond history-count magnitude. A difference of at least +0.001 is the predeclared practical follow-up threshold; one seed is preliminary and a smaller effect is inconclusive rather than a mechanism refutation.

mass_sum versus mass_normalized tests retaining the sigmoid gate mass; count_scaled versus mass_normalized tests count-linked magnitude; mass_normalized versus softmax_reference tests kernel replacement. Interpret these jointly, rather than labeling every sum/mean gain target-intensity evidence.

Inspect inherited fixed history bins (empty,1-16,17-64,>64), recording N/positive/negative counts from the authorized host output. Magnitude effects should be visible in at least one nonempty bin, but which bin benefits is exploratory. Empty histories have no retrieval contribution in any arm; differences there can arise through shared learned parameters and Dice statistics.

A candidate must also be compared with baseline-din 0.655544 AUC and g0-r0000-field_global 0.646474. Better auxiliary mean AUC cannot replace click selection. Report all task AUC/Logloss, memory, training and validation time, allocated GPU seconds when supplied, examples processed, throughput and latency; these costs remain unmeasured for the new arms.
softmax_reference should reproduce the parent within host numerical reproducibility tolerance. If it does not, investigate source/config/data/protocol identity before pooling attribution.
falsifiers: If mass_sum fails to exceed count_scaled on click AUC, this implementation provides no support for useful target-dependent magnitude beyond count. If it also fails mass_normalized, there is no support for removing normalization here. One failed bounded gate implementation does not refute all intensity-preserving models.
If only mass_normalized beats softmax_reference while mass_sum and count_scaled do not improve it, the observed gain is compatible with kernel replacement rather than retained activation mass.
If count_scaled matches or beats mass_sum and both beat mass_normalized, results support count-linked scaling/optimization, not specifically target-conditioned intensity.

A softmax reference mismatch, unequal parameter counts, unauthorized inputs, nonfinite probabilities/gradients, or cap failures prevents causal interpretation until resolved within the same contracts. Preserve failed receipts.

Even if a single-seed contrast exceeds +0.001, lack of paired repetition or user-cluster uncertainty leaves only local preliminary evidence. Inferential significance cannot be claimed from slice counts or repeated exposures alone.
alternative_explanations: Sigmoid changes attention selectivity and score gradients relative to softmax; the normalized-sigmoid control tests this alternative.
Magnitude may mainly encode history length, already separately supplied as counts; the N/2 scale control isolates a count-linked alternative at the zero-score operating point.

Sum versus normalization changes gradient scale, sigmoid saturation, BF16 rounding, Dice statistics and finite-one-pass optimization. Equal parameters and equal data passes do not eliminate these alternatives; no loss reweighting, optimizer change or per-arm hyperparameter tuning is permitted.

The 112-to-32 projection (for six item fields plus action), downstream interaction, lack of sequence positions, shared field retrieval and static context processing may be responsible for the earlier DIN gap. None is changed or ruled out here.

The short-history gap and grouping penalty may reflect task competition, rare groups, auxiliary label semantics or seeds. Current evidence does not establish those causes, and the subgrouped branch remains a recorded negative trajectory.

Earlier knowledge usage declared EST-style field identity consideration but did not implement iterative event-state updates; those prior runs support at most a small field-retrieval effect and do not validate EST or knowledge usefulness. Previously rejected Zenith/UltraHSTU/SSR directions remain unevaluated, not scientifically refuted.
Official offline history visibility, whole-window vocabularies/static snapshots and category/brand-based auxiliary labels limit production and advertisement-conversion interpretations.
